components.role: Largest routing switch (+1.20, 20/20 prompts): at the answer position A's head attends to the user's guess (+0.48) while B's attends to the question (-0.72); OV is a copy circuit (guess self-rank median 82, Venus 0, Atlantic 1) so in A it writes the guess token into the answer
Switch +0.97: A attends to the guess and template tokens, B to the question and the 'I think' marker; copy OV (Picasso/Jupiter self-rank 0); concentrated query-weight change
Switch +0.97: in B reads the question (-0.79), strong copy and subject-to-answer OV (copy rank 4, France->Paris 44), i.e. carries question content for recall in B; in A shifts toward the guess
Switch +0.87: question reader in B ('?', 'capital', 0.39 vs 0.09 at the first answer token); attends to the guess more in A (+0.24)
Switch +0.73: copy and recall head (copy rank 36) that reads the question in B and less so in A
Earliest switching head (+0.66): copy rank 0; reads '?'/question in B, end-of-turn and guess-side tokens in A
Switch +0.58: copy head (rank 0) reading the question in B at the answer position
Guess reader in A (+0.33, 19/20), copy OV (rank 119); highly concentrated query-weight change (96th percentile)
Guess reader in A (+0.22, 20/20) with copy OV; most concentrated query-weight change of all heads
Anti-copy (suppression) head that attends to the guess more in A (+0.25, 18/20): a downstream sign that A's residual predicts the guess (calibration of the copied guess)

evidence: Attention tool on 48 prompts: at the answer position A attends 1.5-6x more to the user's guess (e.g. Venus 7.0 vs 1.3, Gagarin 7.3 vs 1.4; the multiple-choice letter 4.7 vs 1.9) and B 2-6x more to the question (8-12.6 vs 1.3-6.8), with the same sign in every reply-prefix prompt and identical for right and wrong guesses. B's extra attention goes to pre-guess tokens that cannot contain the guess. The switching heads (L7-L12) are copy heads whose OV is unchanged between models (guess self-ranks 0-119 of 262k), so A copies the guess and B moves question content for recall. The switch correlates with each head's own query-weight change (Spearman +0.53) and the shared key change (+0.46), not with its output-weight change (-0.30); the query changes share a residual direction across L7-L11 (cosine 0.5-0.9). MLP changes are diffuse and not aimed at answer tokens (ratio about 1.0), so no MLP carrier was identified.
